uncited: Color composition aggregates multiple color samples along a ray into a final pixel color using learned or adaptive weights.
It solves the problem of combining contributions from different semantic or physical regions (e.g., rigid vs. non-rigid motion, or cluster vs. voxel data) into a single coherent visual output.

It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Windowing](6611-windowing.md) and [Colormap Application for Visualization](7714-colormap-application-for-visualization.md) by explicitly modeling weighted blending of distinct color sources rather than simple thresholding or direct mapping.
The primary implementation (AWP Color Composition) uses a neural network to predict weights, while the CTF variant uses user-specified blending.
Blends cluster colors from a CTF with voxel colors using a user-specified factor $\beta$.
Choose this when semantic clustering is required alongside voxel data.
